title: Ministry of Culture signs agreement with Google Arts & Culture to put heritage collections online
dek: The memorandum covers ASI monuments, national museum holdings, manuscripts documented under Gyan Bharatam and living traditions, with the Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum at its centre.
body: The Union Ministry of Culture signed a memorandum of understanding with Google Arts & Culture on 5 November 2026, the ministry said in a release issued through the Press Information Bureau that evening. The signing took place at a virtual ceremony attended by Vivek Aggarwal, Secretary of the ministry, and Amit Sood, Vice President and Founder of Google Arts & Culture.

According to the ministry, the partnership is meant to span sites and monuments under the Archaeological Survey of India's protection, with their collections, the holdings of the national museums, the manuscripts being documented under the Gyan Bharatam mission, and the crafts, living traditions and performing arts supported by the ministry's institutions.

The ministry places the Yuge Yugeen Bharat Museum, a museum of Indian history taking shape in New Delhi's North and South Blocks, at the centre of the agreement. Digitising it is meant to record both the buildings and the objects they will house, and to give the public an early look at the museum before it opens.

The ministry says it wants people to be able to explore the material in Indian languages, on any device. Sood said the collections would be made "freely discoverable". Google Arts & Culture has worked before with the ASI, the National Museum and the National Gallery of Modern Art.
The release does not give the length of the agreement, a timetable, its cost, which collections will go online first, or how the digital images may be reused.

sources.title: Ministry of Culture signs memorandum of understanding with Google Arts & Culture to digitise and share India's cultural heritage
sources.publisher: Press Information Bureau, Ministry of Culture
